title: C:metabolic-cell (SIBED): catalysis-induced condensates from a random field, each wrapped in a layer of an amphiphile it makes by its own catalysis, divide repeatedly by pinching on a consumed, regrowing fuel and all die within 100 t when fuel regrowth stops
summary: world.py is c40's dividing CIPS world (20261026T1025-c40-cips-turnover-divide-claim: enzyme e drifts up its product p, cat = kc F e^2 (1-p), fuel F consumed and regrown, enzyme turnover d=0.003, random-field start) plus an amphiphile s made only by catalysis (ks_s*cat), adsorbing at the enzyme interface (drift up grad 4e(1-e), chi_s=6) and decaying (0.02); s does not act back. On seeds 0 and 1, 6 and 7 bodies nucleate and divide by dumbbell pinching to generation 3 and 2 (11 and 9 persistent splits, 0 merges; pack/seed*/lineage.png, births_s*.png). Every body carries an s layer at every sampled time: by signed distance to the contour, rim/core >= 5.8 and rim/outside >= 24.5 in 460/460 body-samples (ring_s*.json, 18 times each), labkit radial s rim/core 4.5-4.8 and rim/outside 19 (73/79 and 78/83 individuals), and the layer outlines each dumbbell through the pinch (snaps_s*.png). Stopping fuel regrowth at t=12000 dissolves all 19 bodies within 100 t on both seeds, also with turnover switched off at the fork, while the fed twins keep all 19 (fork_s*.png).

claims.statement: In pack/seed0 and pack/seed1 (world.py defaults, seeds 0 and 1), 6 and 7 enzyme condensates nucleate from a random field spread over the whole box. Each carries a rim layer of the amphiphile s, which is made only by catalysis and mostly by the bodies themselves (49-53% of all catalysis at t=1000, 77-83% at t=8900, snaps_s*_share.json). The bodies and their descendants divide by pinching into two round, layered daughters, repeatedly (generation 3 and 2, 0 merges). Every body depends on the consumed fuel: when fuel regrowth stops at t=12000 all 19 dissolve within 100 t on both seeds, with or without enzyme turnover after the fork, while the fed twins keep all 19.
claims.track: seed 0 (pack/seed0/lineage.png, metrics.json persistent_splits): founder track 1 nucleates at t~200, splits at t=3900 into 12 and 13; 13 splits at t=8900 into 16 and 17; 16 splits at t=16600 into 26 and 27 (generation 3, births_s0.png). Every body on this line carries the s layer at each of the 18 sampled times (ring_s0.json: all bodies pass at every time; snaps_s.png shows the layer around this line's dumbbell), and it dissolves within 100 t of the fuel fork at t=12000 (fork_s0.png) while its fed twin persists

controls_run.E: fork.py from one shared state at t=12000, seeds 0 and 1: fed twin vs kF=0 vs kF=0 with turnover d=0 (fork_s0.png, fork_s1.png, fork_s*_counts.json)
controls_run.B: ring_chis0_s0.json: chi_s=0 (no adsorption), same seed: s peaks in the core (median rim/core 0.65-0.71 over 6 times), 0 of 50 body-samples pass; with ks_s=0 s has no source and stays 0
controls_run.D: parent claim 20261026T1025: dt/2 gives the same division history; Lsc=5 planted founder divides 1->2->4->8

claims.bd_control: chi=0 twin (product-chemotaxis drift removed, enzyme left with linear diffusion and turnover), seed 0, pack_chi0/seed0: 0 bodies to t=6000; the parent claim ran it on seeds 0 and 1 with the same result

limits: B is a quasi-equilibrium adsorbed layer pushed to the interface by a drift written against the body field (grad of 4e(1-e)); the body makes most of s only after t~1000 (49-53% of catalysis at t=1000), and the layer does no work (one-way coupled: e, p, F and the division history are identical with or without s). Division stops once bodies fill the box at the lever-rule area fraction (16-17 bodies; no deaths in the fed world), so births do not continue indefinitely. Division axes lie along the grid diagonals at Lsc=3; the Lsc=5 check (parent claim) used a planted founder without s. Enzyme turnover is a decay term (1/d = 333 t); fork_d0 shows the dissolution does not need it.
